neighbours.label: the second piece of 'forage' / 'forays' (for|age, for|ays): an animal or person going out in search of food or ventures
fire: At dusk the deer leave the woods to forage in the meadow.
Bears forage for berries and roots before winter.
The seabirds make long forays out to sea in search of fish.
In autumn, squirrels forage beneath the oak trees.
His early forays into politics were not successful.
Goats will forage on almost any plant they can reach.
The children made several forays into the kitchen for snacks.
Bees forage over a wide area on warm days.
quiet: At dusk the deer leave the woods to graze in the meadow.
Bears search for berries and roots before winter.
The seabirds make long trips out to sea in search of fish.
We have not seen the old squirrels beneath the oak trees for ages.
His early attempts at politics were not successful.
Goats will eat almost any plant they can reach.
The children made several trips into the kitchen for snacks.
Bees fly over a wide area on warm days.
